Read EPUB books, hear words spoken naturally, look them up offline, and bring your Anki decks along.

## New
- **EPUB books.** They open as clean, reflowing text with their table of contents, in light or dark, and reopen at the spot where you stopped.
- **Words keep their sentence.** Each saved word remembers the sentence you found it in. Review cards and the Words page show it.
- **Pronunciation.** Hear any word or sentence from the word card, in reviews (press P) and on the Words page. The app uses your computer's voices by default. Natural-sounding voices for many languages are a free download in Settings and work offline on Windows, macOS and Linux.
- **Offline dictionaries for 30 languages.** The word card can show definitions, examples and synonyms from Wiktionary. Download the languages you need in Settings → Dictionaries.
- **Other forms of saved words are highlighted.** With a dictionary installed, saving "manger" also highlights "mangé" and "mangeons", and Turkish "ev" also highlights "evde". Clicking one shows which saved word it belongs to.
- **Anki and CSV.** Export any list as an Anki deck (with your review schedule) or as a spreadsheet. You can also import Anki decks, choosing which fields hold the word, translation and example. Everything is under **Import / Export** on the Words page.

## Notes
- Already downloaded a dictionary during testing? Remove it and download it again to get word forms.
- Japanese and Korean have no free natural voice yet, so those use your computer's voices.
- On macOS, the first time you open the app, go to **System Settings → Privacy & Security** and click **Open Anyway**. The Windows build isn't code-signed yet, so SmartScreen may warn the first time.
